newsitem.title: USA: National Semiconductor profits soar in third quarter.
newsitem.headline: National Semiconductor profits soar in third quarter.

text.p: National Semiconductor Corp., a major computer chip manufacturer, said Thursday its profits soared in the third quarter as demand for computers and computer networks continued to grow.
Profits surged to $42.8 million, or 30 cents a share, in the quarter ended Feb. 23 from $23.0 million, or 17 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Sales rose to $680.5 million from $600.3 million.
Sales and earnings also improved over the second quarter, overriding a seasonal dip in sales that Santa Clara, Calif.-based National has seen every year since 1984, it said.
"Our strong revenue and earnings performance for the quarter is one of the early paybacks of our new focus on operational excellence," said Chief Executive Officer Brian Halla.

"Combined with the continuing recovery of our targeted market areas in analogue, Ethernet, wireless and high-end personal computers, this improvement is reflected in our increased bottom line profitability," he said.
Worldwide bookings surged more than 40 percent from last year's third quarter, the company said.
National's stock rose 75 cents to $31.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
